analyst_view.overall: Early view: bottom-half Osasuna (16th) host winless, last-placed Málaga, who lost 2-1 at home to Racing and finished with ten men. Two reports say coach Juanfran Funes's job is in danger, so a change during the break would make this a new manager's first game. Both sides have a midfielder suspended: Jon Moncayola (five yellows) for Osasuna and Adam Aznou (sent off) for Málaga, while Arrasate expects Herrando, Oroz and Del Castillo to be fit.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Málaga had scored nine in 12 league games and Osasuna are not prolific, relying on Budimir and late set pieces (Catena's header levelled with Athletic). A team at the bottom often tightens up in a new manager's first game, so I lean lower.

corners.text: The site expects 10.3 corners. Arrasate's side attack down the wings with Moro, Rubén García and Barja crossing for Budimir, and Málaga defend in a back five. That mix usually brings a steady flow of corners for the home team.

cards.text: The model has 4.6 cards and I lean higher. Málaga collected seven yellows and a red against Racing, and Osasuna committed 19 fouls against Athletic. At the bottom of the table in a loud El Sadar, five or six cards is likely.

shots.text: The site expects 30.6 shots. Osasuna had 17 against Athletic and Málaga average about 11 a game, which adds up to the high 20s. Málaga in a low block will keep many Osasuna attempts from long range.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. Málaga average only about three shots on target a game, and Osasuna's crossing game produces more headers than clean strikes. I see about eight.
